artifactStorageReview.note: The debugger log and regression replay patch are stored as lossless gzip with mtime 0. Decompression reproduces the exact historical bytes and SHA256. Historical emitted receipt paths and diagnostic-assessment metadata retain their original filenames; consult storedPath in the transport manifest to read them.

authorshipBoundary: This reviewer authored the peer shutdown regression and report verifier. Their code review is not independent of authorship; separate peer repair/regression review is retained in diagnostic-assessment.json.

findings.description: Multi-group Linux cleanup could return a passed command when final session enumeration was unavailable or truncated, leaving unseen groups unqualified.
findings.redEvidence: supervisor-unverified-red.log: expected OSError was not raised; exit 1.
findings.repair: Linux cleanup now fails closed for unavailable, truncated or malformed final session enumeration; malformed identity/resource/state rows invalidate enumeration.

limits: Swift executable, build and test evidence is debug configuration, not release performance or release qualification.
Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 / Swift 6.4.1 execution used Rosetta on an aarch64 Colima guest and Apple Silicon host. Native SwiftPM engine and Linux target do not make this native Linux x64 acceptance.
The transport teardown stack and blocked/pending SIGTERM demonstrate the observed local owner. They do not prove the original hosted failure has the identical cause without the pending native probe.

The eight CLI reports are synthetic caller-entry observations, bypassing trusted ingress, Gateway provenance and live Discord. No numerical latency/throughput gate or live-service qualification is claimed.
Linux cleanup ownership covers the admitted session. Escaped sessions remain outside its guarantee; zombies-only receipts prove termination, not reaping by container PID 1.
Hosted CI, native Linux x64 acceptance, push/merge, publication and deployment were not performed by this review.

ownedContainerCleanup.verification: Read-back of retained stop/remove/absence receipts; no new container operation by reviewer.

cleanup.note: All owned adapters closed and joined; NIO public pool counts sampled only afterward.

reviewMethod: Read-only source/diff and retained-evidence inspection; independent JSON/hash/population/receipt calculations. No Swift/native reruns or helper reruns during this final review.

sourceReview.instrumentationDecision: Runtime stage patch remains unapplied. Focused synthetic success plus blocked peer signal masks and transport waitUntilExit stack justify repairing the observed peer owner without changing router/responder/statistics APIs.
sourceReview.peer: The SIGTERM handler is installed before unblocking only SIGTERM and before announcing readiness. Exec launchers isolate signal masks; startup/read/termination waits are finite and cleanup reaps the child and checks port closure.
sourceReview.supervisor: Linux admission creates a new session. Cleanup enumerates that session and signals distinct child groups before the leader, preserves a finite TERM/KILL/reap allowance, and rejects unverifiable final enumeration. Real child/grandchild fixtures cover timeout, exited parent, success with hidden output, supervisor interruption and an unrelated session. The heartbeat fixture makes its marker ready before starting cadence measurement.
sourceReview.synthetic: All eight direct/DSL cases remain. Exact offered/admitted/completed parity and individual handler/acknowledgement/byte cleanup assertions are present. Both deferred cancellation paths join the task after confirmed callback and assert one terminal, no edit and no replacement cohort. All eight pre-cancelled paths assert no work. AsyncStream completion/cancellation removes the non-cancellation-aware continuation barrier owner.
